descriptions.text: Earth Hobby Potion. Per subsection 1256-C of the Indigenous Species Protection Act, this particular reward is required by the Syndicate Government to be awarded to all Crawlers who have chosen a domestic class. Taking this potion is optional, however it may not be sold or transferred to other Crawlers or entities. Upon drinking this, you will immediately obtain a Level Three skill ability in a unique, Earth-based hobby. The benefit is chosen at random, however you will not receive a skill that you currently have. Gods, I hate it when the lawyers make me put their crap into the descriptions. Don't you? …

beats.headline: Required by law
beats.text: Donut's Earth box holds a scented candle labelled Sea Breeze that smells nothing like the sea, a cat tree larger and fancier than her old one, and an Earth Hobby Potion. The description cites subsection 1256-C of the Indigenous Species Protection Act: the Syndicate Government requires one for every crawler with a domestic class. Drink it, and gain level three in a random Earth hobby. It could be Parkour. It could be Kombucha Brewing. Carl's Earth box holds one too, beside a three-inch cactus from Home Depot and a pack of eighteen paperback westerns.

beats.headline: Scutelliphily and Cesta Punta
beats.text: Donut drinks hers, glows, and makes a face. Scutelliphily. She doesn't even know what it means; she is a scutelliphile, which sounds obscene. What a waste. Carl clicks his in his hotlist and feels a warmth spread through him. Level 3 in the Cesta Punta skill, and no other explanation. Was that a martial art? He doesn't feel any different. It's likely the art of cracking nuts with your toes, Donut says, and, laughing, asks Gordo the bopca for walnuts so they can experiment.

beats.headline: Jai-alai
beats.text: Running his hand down the wicker-looking basket from his fan box, Carl's mind races, and it all comes rushing to him from that Earth Hobby Potion. Cesta Punta is not a martial art. It is a sport, more commonly known as jai-alai: a complicated, fast-paced, squash-like game in which players wear scoops on their hands and throw balls against a wall, dangerous enough to knock your head off even in a helmet. The scoop a player wears is a xistera, and that is what the fans have voted him.

beats.headline: A gear head
beats.text: Katia tells Carl what she can do. She has no useful spells. She is immune to wind spell damage. She is also good at fixing engines, though she was never a mechanic and has never actually fixed one: she got her Earth Hobby Potion, and she is a gear head. Before all this she was an art teacher, which Carl, looking at her poorly sculpted face, finds hard to credit. She smiles sheepishly.

beats.headline: Engines on demand
beats.text: Putting the vehicle's track mechanism together with Carl, Katia credits the hobby potion. She was sitting there wondering how they were going to build it, and suddenly it was there, like that Matrix movie. Carl's cesta punta translates well into action, he says, but it is mostly muscle. Donut's is still a mystery. Scutelliphily. He has asked a hundred people, and nobody knows what the hell it is.

beats.headline: Small shields
beats.text: Carl thinks he has finally worked out Donut's hobby. He pats his bomb patch: what type of thread is on this thing? Something to do with embroidery or patches, he says, and Donut gasps that he's right. Britney supplies the rest. Scutellus is Latin for small shield, phileein the Greek for the love of, so it means the love of small shields. Donut loves little patches. If anyone had asked, Britney says, she could have told them earlier.
